_comment: EXT-63 SMOKE, arm 12 — SINGLE-LAYER alternative to arm 10 (user direction, 2026-08-04):
kill iono layer 2 outright instead of pinning its level.  layer2_max_degree: 0; the a00
GIM anchor and the rxcb datum stay as in arms 9-11.
WHY (vs arm 10's L2 pin): (1) the grading reference — the COD GIM — IS a single thin
shell at 450 km, so single-layer makes the level directly commensurate, no summed-shell
bookkeeping; (2) arm 9's lesson is that the confounded level tension re-routes to the
loosest level-like direction — REMOVING the direction is strictly stronger than pinning
it; (3) the dual-layer field earned its keep on the SELF-CONTAINED lineage (Iono-2
mech-A, representation) — EXT-CB's question is level realization, and the second shell
adds nothing this campaign needs.  Keep dual-layer where it was validated.
PREDICTION (stated before the run): reproduces arm 10's layer-1 dynamics — ignition
~24 (arm 10: 23.9), dip through the ignition era, upward inflection by ~ep 16, deg-1
dipole peak ~ep 6 then decay, sh_health gate 0/0/0, a00_in_band 20/20 — because arm
10's L2 pin (info 4.0/ep) had already effectively blocked the escape, so removing the
shell should be dynamically near-equivalent.  If it matches, single-layer + a00 GIM
anchor + rxcb datum is the CANONICAL EXT-CB posture and the next 1 h validation runs
this shape.  A material mismatch means the L2 shell was interacting with the pump
beyond its level dof — name it before choosing.
20 epochs is inside ignition: LEVEL + gate wiring read only, no settled-science claim.
